items.stem: Retrieval often returns half of the relevant passage, cutting off mid-explanation. The most direct chunking fix is:

options.text: Add overlap between chunks so boundary meaning is preserved
options.rationale: Correct: overlap keeps context that spans a boundary from being lost.
Metadata removal does not address boundary cut-off.

options.text: Switch to a larger language model
options.rationale: The passage was never retrieved whole; model size is not the fix.
Deleting the index does not address chunk boundaries.

items.explanation: Correct: overlap keeps context that spans a boundary from being lost.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are good reasons to choose hybrid (keyword + vector) indexing? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Exact terms and codes matter and must match precisely
options.rationale: Correct: keyword matching captures exact identifiers vectors may miss.

options.text: Semantic paraphrases must also be retrieved
options.rationale: Correct: vector search captures meaning beyond exact words.

options.text: You want to remove all metadata
options.rationale: Metadata is unrelated to the hybrid rationale.
Hybrid does not reduce the need for evaluation.

items.explanation: Correct: keyword matching captures exact identifiers vectors may miss.

items.stem: A new chunking strategy answered one demo question better. What should you conclude?

options.text: Nothing yet; evaluate on a representative test set before concluding
options.rationale: Correct: one query is not evidence; honest evaluation needs a test set.

options.text: The new strategy is definitively better
options.rationale: A single query cannot establish that.
That does not follow from one result.

items.explanation: Correct: one query is not evidence; honest evaluation needs a test set.
